questions.question: Identify which of the following sentences is in Passive Voice:

options.text: The Chief Justice inspected the computerized filing section yesterday.
The computer operator is entering the litigant details into the portal.
The certified copies of the judgment were dispatched this morning.
The advocate will file an urgent special leave petition tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Sentence (C) mein subject 'The certified copies of the judgment' action ka doer nahi balki receiver hai. Isme verb phrase 'were dispatched' ('be' ka form 'were' + V3 'dispatched') hai, jo Passive Voice ka standard marker hai. Option (A), (B), aur (D) mein subjects ('The Chief Justice', 'The computer operator', 'The advocate') khud actions kar rahe hain, isliye wo Active Voice mein hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Passive voice = Object as Subject + form of 'be' + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.subtopic: Fill in the Blanks — Present Continuous
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct passive verb form:
'Do not enter courtroom number four; the digital recording setup ___ by the technicians right now.'

options.text: is being tested
is tested
was being tested
has been tested

questions.explanation: Sentence mein time marker 'right now' aur imperative warning 'Do not enter' present continuous aspect ko establish karte hain. Subject 'the digital recording setup' singular noun hai, isliye Present Continuous passive formula 'is + being + V3' ➔ 'is being tested' (A) sahi hai. Option (B) Simple Present hai, Option (C) Past tense hai, aur Option (D) completed action (Perfect) hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Present Continuous Passive = is/am/are + being + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The high court protocol officer receives the visiting dignitaries at the airport.'

options.text: The visiting dignitaries were received by the high court protocol officer at the airport.
The visiting dignitaries are received by the high court protocol officer at the airport.
The visiting dignitaries are being received by the high court protocol officer at the airport.
The visiting dignitaries have been received by the high court protocol officer at the airport.

questions.explanation: Active verb 'receives' Simple Present tense mein hai. Naya subject 'The visiting dignitaries' plural noun hai. Simple Present passive mein plural subject ke sath 'are + V3' lagta hai: 'are received' (B). Option (A) Simple Past ('were received') mein tense change karta hai. Option (C) continuous hai aur Option (D) perfect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Simple Present Passive = Plural Subject + are + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.subtopic: Simple Past with Plural Object Shift
questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The forensic expert examined the disputed signatures carefully.'

options.text: The disputed signatures was examined by the forensic expert carefully.
The disputed signatures were examined by the forensic expert carefully.
The disputed signatures had been examined by the forensic expert carefully.
The disputed signatures were being examined by the forensic expert carefully.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Simple Past ('examined', V2) mein hai. Naya subject 'The disputed signatures' plural noun hai. Isliye passive auxiliary 'were' lagegi: 'were examined' (B). Option (A) mein plural subject ke sath singular 'was' laga diya gaya hai jo agreement error hai. Option (C) Past Perfect hai aur Option (D) Past Continuous hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Simple Past Passive = Plural Object + were + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The postman has delivered all the judicial summons.'

options.text: All the judicial summons has been delivered by the postman.
All the judicial summons have been delivered by the postman.
All the judicial summons were delivered by the postman.
All the judicial summons had been delivered by the postman.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Present Perfect ('has delivered') mein hai. Active subject singular ('postman') tha, lekin naya subject 'All the judicial summons' plural noun hai (summons singular bhi hota hai aur plural mein yahan 'all' ke sath plural sense hai). Isliye plural auxiliary 'have been delivered' (B) correct hai. Option (A) mein 'has been' lagaya gaya hai jo agreement error hai. Option (C) Simple Past hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Present Perfect Passive = Plural Subject + have been + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The stenographer was typing the confidential statements.'

options.text: The confidential statements was being typed by the stenographer.
The confidential statements were typed by the stenographer.
The confidential statements were being typed by the stenographer.
The confidential statements had been typed by the stenographer.

questions.explanation: Active verb 'was typing' Past Continuous hai aur naya subject 'The confidential statements' plural noun hai. Isliye plural auxiliary 'were' + continuous marker 'being' + V3 'typed' ➔ 'were being typed' (C) sahi answer hai. Option (A) mein singular 'was' laga hai, Option (B) mein 'being' omit hai, aur Option (D) Past Perfect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Past Continuous Passive = Plural Object + were + being + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The appellate bench had dismissed the writ petition before the summer vacation.'

options.text: The writ petition was dismissed by the appellate bench before the summer vacation.
The writ petition had been dismissed by the appellate bench before the summer vacation.
The writ petition has been dismissed by the appellate bench before the summer vacation.
The writ petition had dismissed by the appellate bench before the summer vacation.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Past Perfect ('had dismissed') mein hai. Past Perfect passive ka universal formula hai: 'had + been + V3'. Isliye 'had been dismissed' (B) correct hai. Option (A) Simple Past hai, Option (C) Present Perfect hai, aur Option (D) mein 'been' omit kar diya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Past Perfect Passive = Object + had + been + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The vigilance committee will investigate the financial irregularities.'

options.text: The financial irregularities would be investigated by the vigilance committee.
The financial irregularities will be investigated by the vigilance committee.
The financial irregularities will investigated by the vigilance committee.
The financial irregularities will have been investigated by the vigilance committee.

questions.explanation: Active verb 'will investigate' Simple Future tense mein hai. Simple Future passive formula: 'will/shall + be + V3' ➔ 'will be investigated' (B). Option (A) mein 'will' ko 'would' mein backshift kiya gaya hai jo Voice mein strictly forbidden hai. Option (C) mein 'be' omit hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Simple Future Passive = will / shall + be + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The dispatcher will have sent the notifications by Friday.'

options.text: The notifications will be sent by the dispatcher by Friday.
The notifications will have been sent by the dispatcher by Friday.
The notifications will has been sent by the dispatcher by Friday.
The notifications would have been sent by the dispatcher by Friday.

questions.explanation: Active verb 'will have sent' Future Perfect tense mein hai. Future Perfect passive formula: 'will have been + V3' ➔ 'will have been sent' (B). Option (A) Simple Future hai. Option (C) mein modal ke baad 'has' lagaya gaya hai jo ungrammatical hai. Option (D) conditional would use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Future Perfect Passive = will / shall + have + been + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The appellant has not submitted the certified copies of the decree.'

options.text: The certified copies of the decree has not been submitted by the appellant.
The certified copies of the decree have not been submitted by the appellant.
The certified copies of the decree were not submitted by the appellant.
The certified copies of the decree have been not submitted by the appellant.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Present Perfect Negative ('has not submitted') mein hai. Naya subject 'The certified copies' plural noun hai, isliye plural auxiliary 'have' lagegi. Negative particle 'not' first auxiliary ke baad lagega: 'have not been submitted' (B). Option (A) mein plural subject ke sath singular 'has' laga hai. Option (D) mein 'not' ki position galat hai ('have been not').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03 & RC-08: Negative auxiliary chain = have + NOT + been + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'The scrutiny clerk did not accept the defective memo of appeal.'

options.text: The defective memo of appeal was not accepted by the scrutiny clerk.
The defective memo of appeal did not accepted by the scrutiny clerk.
The defective memo of appeal had not been accepted by the scrutiny clerk.
The defective memo of appeal is not accepted by the scrutiny clerk.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Simple Past Negative ('did not accept') mein hai. Naya subject 'The defective memo of appeal' singular noun hai. Simple Past passive negative formula: 'was not + V3' ➔ 'was not accepted' (A). Option (B) ungrammatical 'did not accepted' use karta hai. Option (C) Past Perfect hai aur Option (D) Present tense hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04 & RC-08: Simple Past Negative Passive = was / were + not + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'Did the registrar approve the casual leave application?'

options.text: Did the casual leave application approved by the registrar?
Was the casual leave application approved by the registrar?
Had the casual leave application been approved by the registrar?
Is the casual leave application approved by the registrar?

questions.explanation: Active sentence Simple Past Yes/No question ('Did + Subject + V1?') hai. Passive banate waqt 'Did' gayab ho jata hai aur naye singular subject 'the casual leave application' ke mutabiq Simple Past auxiliary 'Was' shuru mein aati hai: 'Was the casual leave application approved by the registrar?' (B). Option (A) 'Did' retain karta hai jo galat hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Simple Past Yes/No Interrogative = Was / Were + Object + V3 + (by + Subject)?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'Why did the single bench stay the demolition order?'

options.text: Why the demolition order was stayed by the single bench?
Why was the demolition order stayed by the single bench?
Why had the demolition order been stayed by the single bench?
Why is the demolition order stayed by the single bench?

questions.explanation: Wh-questions mein interrogative word order mandatory hota hai: Wh-word + auxiliary + new subject + V3. Yahan 'Why' ke turant baad auxiliary 'was' aayegi, fir naya subject 'the demolition order', aur fir V3 'stayed': 'Why was the demolition order stayed by the single bench?' (B). Option (A) mein assertive word order ('Why the demolition order was...') use kiya gaya hai jo direct question mein fatal error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Wh-word + auxiliary + Object + V3 + (by + Subject)? Assertive order strictly galat hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform into Passive Voice:
'Who prepared this confidential chargesheet?'

options.text: By whom this confidential chargesheet was prepared?
By whom was this confidential chargesheet prepared?
Who was this confidential chargesheet prepared by?
By whom had this confidential chargesheet been prepared?

questions.explanation: Active 'Who' sentence ka subject hai. Passive mein 'Who' agent ban kar 'By whom' ban jata hai. Iske turant baad auxiliary verb ka inversion aana zaroori hai: 'By whom + was + Object + V3?'. Isliye (B) correct hai. Option (A) mein inversion nahi hai ('this chargesheet was'). Option (C) informal conversational English hai, jabki competitive exam answer keys mein 'By whom' standard primary answer hota hai. Option (D) tense badal deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: 'Who + V2 + O?' ➔ 'By whom + was/were + O + V3?'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate and natural Passive Voice form:
'The police arrested the notorious extortionist yesterday.'

options.text: The notorious extortionist was arrested by the police yesterday.
The notorious extortionist was arrested yesterday.
The notorious extortionist has been arrested yesterday.
The notorious extortionist had been arrested yesterday.

questions.explanation: Arrest karne ka action sirf police authority dwara hi legally kiya ja sakta hai. English grammar aur high-level competitive exams mein obvious professional agents ('by the police', 'by doctors') ko omit karna stylistically superior aur correct mana jata hai. Isliye (B) 'The notorious extortionist was arrested yesterday' standard natural passive hai. Option (C) yesterday ke sath present perfect use karta hai jo wrong hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & Section G: Obvious/natural agents ko standard formal passive mein omit kiya jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question: Which of the following sentences CANNOT form a valid Passive Voice construction?

options.text: The defense witness arrived at the high court premises on time.
The bench reserved the final judgment.
The computer operator cleared the printer queue.
The police recovered the missing case dairy.

questions.explanation: Sentence (A) mein verb 'arrived' intransitive verb hai. 'Arrived' ke baad 'at the premises' place batata hai (prepositional adverb phrase), direct object nahi. Chunki koi direct object nahi hai, isliye iska passive banana impossible hai ('The premises was arrived' pure non-English syntax hai). Baaki teeno sentences (B, C, D) mein transitive verbs ('reserved', 'cleared', 'recovered') hain jinke objects ('the final judgment', 'the printer queue', 'the missing case dairy') maujood hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & Section H: Intransitive verbs (arrive, sleep, die, go, laugh) lack a direct object and cannot form passive voice.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Spot the grammatically incorrect part of the sentence:
'(A) The revised administrative guidelines / (B) were circular / (C) to all district registry offices / (D) yesterday morning.'

options.text: (A) The revised administrative guidelines
(B) were circular
(C) to all district registry offices
(D) yesterday morning

questions.explanation: Part (B) mein galti hai. Sentence Passive Voice mein hai ('guidelines were...'). Passive voice mein helping verb 'were' ke baad main verb ki Past Participle (V3) form aani chahiye. Yahan noun/adjective 'circular' likh diya gaya hai, jabki sahi verb form 'circulated' (V3) honi chahiye: 'were circulated to all district registry offices'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Passive voice mandates Past Participle V3 form: were + circulated (NOT were circular).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.subtopic: Pronoun Case Shift in Agentive Phrase
questions.question:
Choose the grammatically correct Passive Voice conversion:
'He drafted the entire administrative rejoinder.'

options.text: The entire administrative rejoinder was drafted by he.
The entire administrative rejoinder was drafted by him.
The entire administrative rejoinder was drafted by his.
The entire administrative rejoinder had drafted by him.

questions.explanation: Preposition 'by' ke baad hamesha pronoun ka Objective Case lagta hai. Pronoun 'He' (Subjective) ka objective form 'him' hota hai ('by him', not 'by he' or 'by his'). Isliye (B) correct answer hai. Option (A) mein subjective case 'he' lagaya gaya hai jo grammatical error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Section B: Pronoun case transformation: He ➔ by him, She ➔ by her, They ➔ by them.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Transform the following Passive sentence into Active Voice:
'The digital court records were inspected by the chief auditor.'

options.text: The chief auditor inspects the digital court records.
The chief auditor was inspecting the digital court records.
The chief auditor inspected the digital court records.
The chief auditor had inspected the digital court records.

questions.explanation: Passive sentence mein verb phrase 'were inspected' hai jo Simple Past Passive ko indicate karta hai. Active Voice banate waqt agent 'the chief auditor' subject banega aur verb Simple Past active form (V2) 'inspected' ban jayegi: 'The chief auditor inspected the digital court records.' (C). Option (A) Simple Present hai, Option (B) Past Continuous hai, aur Option (D) Past Perfect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Reverse rule: was/were + V3 ➔ Active Simple Past (V2).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Convert the following sentence into Passive Voice:
'The registry returned the writ petition because the petitioner did not affix the requisite court fee stamp.'

options.text: The writ petition was returned by the registry because the requisite court fee stamp was not affixed by the petitioner.
The writ petition had been returned by the registry because the requisite court fee stamp had not been affixed.
The writ petition was returned by the registry because the petitioner did not affix the requisite court fee stamp.
The writ petition is returned by the registry because the requisite court fee stamp is not affixed by the petitioner.

questions.explanation: Complex sentence mein do coordinated actions hain aur dono Simple Past mein hain ('returned' aur 'did not affix'). Dono transitive clauses ka parallel passive banega: 1. 'The writ petition was returned by the registry', 2. 'because the requisite court fee stamp was not affixed by the petitioner'. Dono clauses mein Simple Past passive auxiliary 'was / was not' lag kar (A) bilkul flawless complete transformation banata hai. Option (B) dono ko Past Perfect bana deta hai jo galat hai. Option (D) Present tense mein distort kar deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04 & RC-08: Multi-clause sentences mein har transitive clause ka voice aur tense parallel preserve kiya jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04
